questions.question: Explain with example each the following a. Long term borrowings and short-term borrowings b Provisions and short-term provisions c. Trade payables and trade receivables / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Long-term borrowings And Short-term borrowings Long-term Borrowings are loans or debts that are repayable after more than 12 months . They are shown under non-current liabilities in the Balance Sheet. Short-term Borrowings are loans that must be repaid within 12 months. They are shown under current liabilities. Provisions and short term provisions: These are liabilities of uncertain amount or timing. They are created to cover expected future expenses or losses. Can be long-term or short- term, depending on when they are expected to be settled. Trade Payables vs Trade Receivables Trade Payables: Amounts a business owes to suppliers for goods or services purchased on credit. It is a liability and includes Creditors and Bills Payables Trade Receivables : Amounts owed to the business by customers for goods or services sold on credit. It is an asset and includes Debtors and Bills receivables.
